clues: This is a coastal town in Leyte, in the Philippines. It lies south of Tacloban and faces a gulf.
Rain falls here all year, with no clear dry season. The wettest months run from November to January, when typhoons can flood some home areas.
In 1954, a big group of small villages split away. They formed a new town with the name Mayorga.
This town rose from the ruins of the Second World War. It did not just survive that hard time; it grew and thrived.
People know this place by a nickname from its war story. They call it the Liberation Town.
